rationale: C08 is the only displayed candidate containing the same specialized loyalty-removal framework and closely corresponding decisional-standard language. Its rule makes separation turn on whether “reasonable grounds exist for a belief” that an officer is disloyal; the child revises the government-wide standard so refusal or removal turns on whether the evidence creates “a reasonable doubt” as to loyalty. That concrete reformulation of the same evidentiary test plausibly supplied material drafting language and structure. C05 has a more general personnel-separation mechanism, and C19 exemplifies a concise amendment format, but neither approaches C08’s substantive overlap.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The standard for the refusal of employment or the removal from employment ... on grounds relating to loyalty shall be that, on all the evidence, there is a reasonable doubt as to the loyalty of the person involved to the Government of the United States.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: If the Administrator finds, in accordance with the standards and procedures prescribed by ... [the employee loyalty directive] ... that reasonable grounds exist for a belief that an officer of the Service is disloyal to the Government of the United States, such officer shall be separated from the Service.
shared_material.explanation: Both provisions define the evidentiary standard governing adverse personnel action for suspected disloyalty, using closely parallel “reasonable” belief-or-doubt language and the same loyalty-to-the-Government formulation.
